lead: `<`/`<=`/`>`/`>=`/`<=>` over two `string`s is `E0715` where it is written, and the diagnostic names the member that says what was meant.
body: `Core\Str::compare` is the ordering two strings have; the same code refuses a `bytes`, an `array<T>`, a `callable`, an enum case (order `as int` instead) and `null`, while the object family keeps `E0411`. A case asserting text ordering asserts `Core\Str::compare`, and one wanting a fixed slice still uses `==`; a `Core` member answering `uint` (`Core\Str::length`) in `$int + …` is `E0407`, not a widening.
